newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Japan's Mitsui to fix Uzbek oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Mitsui to fix Uzbek oil refinery.

text.p: Japan's Mitsui & Company Ltd signed a contract on Monday to carry out a $200 million upgrade of Uzbekistan's Fergana oil refinery, a spokesman for the company said.
"The contract was signed today in Tokyo with (state energy concern) Uzbekneftegaz," the Mitsui representative, who declined to be named, told reporters in the Uzbek capital Tashkent.

Japan's Eximbank will provide a $120 million credit for the installation of hydrosulphide refining technology with a 1.7 million-tonne annual capacity at the plant, located 300 km (200 miles) north of the capital Tashkent.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will provide the remaining $80 million.

The Fergana refinery has an annual capacity of around six million tonnes. The upgrade is needed in part to convert the refinery so that it can process more crude oil from Uzbekistan's Kokdumalak field.
A second oil refinery in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region, with a capacity of five million tonnes a year, is now under construction by French firm Technip.
The desert nation of 23-million aims to be self-sufficient in petroleum products.
